request: We should know which of our contacts are most influential so we can prioritize them.
gaps: What specific criteria will be used to determine a contact's influence score?
Who will have access to view the influence scores of contacts?
What safeguards are in place to protect potentially sensitive data related to influence scoring?
How will the system handle situations where contacts or roles change?
How frequently will influence scores be updated?

proposals.summary: This release will implement a system for identifying and ranking our contacts based on their influence. It will be used by regional coordinators and project managers to prioritize engagement with key government representatives.

core_commitments.text: Provide a ranked list of contacts based on their influence.
Allow users to filter and segment contacts for targeted engagement.

in_scope.text: Develop an influence scoring system that assigns scores from 1 to 10 to each contact based on predefined criteria such as position, past project involvement, and engagement frequency.
Create an interface for users to view contacts with their influence scores displayed.
Implement sorting functionality to allow users to view contacts in order of influence scores.
Enable a filtering system to categorize contacts by region and active projects.
Ensure that all data handling complies with existing data protection regulations.

out_of_scope.text: This release will not include a detailed analysis of influence dynamics or predictive modeling for future influence.
User training and documentation for the new feature will not be included in this release.
Integration with external databases to gather additional data points about contacts will not be included.

assumptions.text: Users have access rights to view and manage contact data within the CRM.
assumptions.why_implicit: The feature requires users to interact with sensitive data stored in the CRM.

assumptions.text: Data regarding contact roles and previous engagements is accurately maintained within the system.
assumptions.why_implicit: The influence scoring system relies on accurate and up-to-date information about contacts.

assumptions.text: Existing data protection regulations are understood and adhered to by the organization during implementation.
assumptions.why_implicit: Data processing and assessment of influence scores need to comply with regulations.

definitions.definition: A method of ranking contacts from 1 to 10 based on their perceived impact, determined by factors including but not limited to their role in government, involvement in projects, and frequency of communication.
The ability of a contact to affect decisions or policies within their government or agency, assessed through historical engagement data.

success_criteria.metric: Percentage of users able to identify top 10 influential contacts within 5 minutes of using the feature.
success_criteria.measurement: User feedback and usability testing results.
